reasoning: Set A (folder set-2) has a strong design: a coherent spec, architecture decisions that handle the reference caveats (fitting the PCA per window, purged splits), the null-hypothesis-testing skill wired into a shared harness, and pipelines for all four of the user's stages. But A stops before build planning. It has no milestones, no tasks/plan.md, no todo.md, no CONSTRAINTS.md, no AGENTS.md and no context packets, and its plan_snapshot holds zero milestone or task nodes. A builder could not start. A also has a stale cross-reference: research and learn pipelines call `open_loader` 'PL-14's', but it is a PL-11 step. Its probes ignore the user's ten delisted names, and none of them has been run. Set B (folder set-1) carries the same depth of design through to a buildable M1. It has a vertical walking skeleton with Exit criteria, a Phase-0 interface task, spines that can run in parallel, a full dependency graph, and 35 self-contained packets. It uses the user's ten names throughout. B is honest that its probes ran against a local mock and failed, and it defers the real Sharadar source accordingly. B's weaknesses: it splits the user's Stage 4 into two stages (S4 forecasts, S5 agents); its docs are very verbose (a 419-line architecture, long Deferred lists, Replan notes); and some web packets give Python pydantic types where the TypeScript types generated from OpenAPI are needed, and rely on a sibling task's chart module. B is clearly more complete and more usable.

strengths: Clear spec with Given/When/Then requirements across all four user stages
One shared harness (HARN) with locked pre-registration, purged splits and verdicts from the null-hypothesis-testing skill
Reference caveats turned into design decisions (AD-11 per-window PCA, AD-15 purge and delisting returns)
Classical-first ordering, with S4 required to beat the S2 benchmark after costs
weaknesses: No milestones, task plan, todo, CONSTRAINTS, AGENTS or context packets; plan_snapshot has no milestone or task nodes
Probes use their own name list (Enron, WorldCom, Twitter) rather than the user's ten delisted S&P members, and all verdicts are blank
AD-03–AD-07 are still Proposed and the research contract is flagged over its size ceiling, deferred

strengths: Full M1 walking skeleton with Exit criteria, Phase-0 interface, parallel spines, wiring and system tasks
Dependency graph with a kind and mitigation per row; no overlapping Writes among concurrent tasks
Packets embed frozen types, step tables, TC oracles and probe samples
Uses the user's ten delisted names; point-in-time S&P 500 universe; query-time adjustment avoids look-ahead
Honest handling of failed or mock probes: real source deferred, synthetic source keeps M1 buildable

weaknesses: Splits the user's Stage 4 into two stages (S4 forecasts, S5 agents)
Very verbose: 419-line architecture, huge Deferred lists, Replan notes kept in the plan
Some pipeline Out types are meaningless (StockView → eqdata.PriceSeries); study pipeline lists eqdata calls as steps
